title: Saying no: negation
summary: No before the verb, and the double negative with nada, nadie, nunca.
focus: Negative sentences with no; nada, nadie, nunca, tampoco, ni…ni
content:
## No before the verb

To make a sentence negative, put **no** directly before the verb:

- *No hablo francés.* (I don't speak French.)
- *Ana no vive aquí.* (Ana doesn't live here.)
- *No, no tengo hambre.* (No, I'm not hungry. The first *no* answers and the second negates.)

Spanish needs nothing else: no *do* and no *not*.

## The negative words

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **nada** | nothing | *No quiero nada.* |
| **nadie** | nobody | *No hay nadie.* |
| **nunca** | never | *No como nunca carne.* |
| **tampoco** | neither, not either | *Yo tampoco.* |
| **ningún / ninguna** | no, not any | *No tengo ningún problema.* |
| **ni … ni** | neither … nor | *No bebo ni café ni té.* |

## The double negative is correct

When the negative word comes **after** the verb, *no* stays before the verb: *No veo nada.* (literally "I don't see nothing") is the correct Spanish.

If the negative word comes **before** the verb, drop *no*: *Nunca como carne. Nadie viene. Nada es fácil.*

## Agreeing with a negative

- *No me gusta el café.* *A mí tampoco.* (Me neither.)
- *Me gusta el té.* *A mí también.* (Me too.)

*Tampoco* answers a negative; *también* answers a positive.

quiz.explanation: No goes directly before the conjugated verb.

quiz.prompt: Complete: No quiero ___. (I don't want anything.)
quiz.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anything' is nada.
With nadie after the verb, no stays before it: the double negative is correct.
When nunca comes first, drop no.
hints: Negative word first, so no no.

quiz.prompt: — No me gusta el fútbol. — A mí ___.
quiz.explanation: To agree with a negative, use tampoco.

quiz.prompt: — Me gusta el cine. — A mí ___.
quiz.explanation: To agree with a positive, use también.

quiz.prompt: Complete: No bebo ___ café ___ té. (neither… nor)
quiz.explanation: Neither… nor is ni… ni, with ni before each thing: no bebo ni café ni té. O… o means either… or.
Before a masculine singular noun, ninguno shortens to ningún.

listening.text: No tengo ningún hermano.
listening.meaning: I don't have any brothers.
listening.note: Ningún before a masculine singular noun.

listening.text: Nunca llego tarde a clase.
listening.meaning: I never arrive late to class.
listening.note: Nunca before the verb: no extra no.

listening.text: ¿Quieres algo de beber? No, gracias.
listening.meaning: Do you want something to drink? No, thanks.

listening.text: No hablo ni francés ni alemán.
listening.meaning: I speak neither French nor German.

listening.text: No veo a nadie en el parque.
listening.meaning: I don't see anyone in the park.

listening.text: Yo no bebo café y mi hermana tampoco.
listening.meaning: I don't drink coffee and neither does my sister.

listening.text: Siempre desayuno en casa, pero hoy no tengo tiempo.
listening.meaning: I always have breakfast at home, but today I don't have time.

listening.text: Mi hermano siempre tiene hambre, pero yo no quiero comer nada ahora.
listening.meaning: My brother is always hungry, but I don't want to eat anything now.

bites.title: No goes first
bites.rule: To say no, put no right before the verb. There is no 'do' and no 'not' to add.

bites.title: Two negatives are fine
bites.rule: Spanish uses the double negative. If nada, nadie or nunca comes after the verb, no still stays before it. 'I don't see nothing' is perfect Spanish.

bites.title: Negative first, drop the no
bites.rule: Only one negative word may stand in front of the verb. Put nunca, nadie or nada first and drop no.

bites.title: Tampoco vs también
bites.rule: Agree with a yes using también, and agree with a no using tampoco. A negative pairs with a negative: 'Me neither' is yo tampoco.
bites.example_meaning: — I don't have any money. — Me neither.

sorts.title: Does the blank need 'no'?
sorts.why: If the negative word comes after the verb, no goes before the verb. If the negative word comes first, it already does the job.

sorts.title: Me too or me neither?
sorts.why: También agrees with a positive statement, and tampoco agrees with a negative one.

sorts.title: Positive or negative word?
sorts.why: After a negative verb Spanish uses nada/nadie. Positive sentences and open questions use algo/alguien.

spots.why: After a negative verb, 'anyone' is nadie: the double negative is correct.

spots.sentence: — No me gusta el fútbol. — A mí también.
spots.why: To agree with a negative, use tampoco.
Before a masculine singular noun, ninguno shortens to ningún.

spots.sentence: No bebo o café ni té.
spots.why: Neither… nor is ni… ni, with the same word twice.

builds.text: No bebo ni café ni té.
builds.meaning: I drink neither coffee nor tea.

realm.content:
## No en Eldmark

**No** goes before the verb, and the rest of the sentence stays negative: **no tengo nada de oro**, **no hay nadie en la posada**, **nunca entro solo en la mazmorra**. For neither this nor that, use ni: **no soy ni orco ni elfo, soy minotauro**.

vocabulary.example: No hay nadie en la posada.
Nunca entro solo en la mazmorra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I never enter the dungeon alone.
I don't have a mount either.

vocabulary.example: No soy ni orco ni elfo, soy minotauro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I'm neither an orc nor an elf, I'm a minotaur.

bites.title: No en Eldmark
bites.rule: No goes before the verb, and the rest of the sentence stays negative: no tengo nada, no hay nadie, no voy nunca.
bites.example: No hay nadie en la posada y no tengo nada de oro.
bites.example_meaning: There's nobody at the inn and I have no gold at all.

listening.text: El minotauro no tiene ninguna espada.
listening.meaning: The minotaur doesn't have any sword.

listening.text: Nadie entra en la mazmorra de noche.
listening.meaning: Nobody enters the dungeon at night.
listening.note: Nadie before the verb takes no no.

listening.text: La maga nunca está en la posada.
listening.meaning: The mage is never at the inn.

listening.text: El minotauro no tiene ni oro ni montura.
listening.meaning: The minotaur has neither gold nor a mount.

listening.text: La elfa no tiene botín, y yo tampoco.
listening.meaning: The elf has no loot, and neither do I.

builds.text: No hay nadie en la posada.
Nunca entro solo en la mazmorra.
builds.meaning: I never enter the dungeon alone.

spots.why: After no, stay negative with nada.

spots.sentence: No hay alguien en la posada.

sorts.title: Positive or negative word?
sorts.why: Algo, alguien and siempre are positive; nada, nadie and nunca are their negatives.

meadowbrook.content:
## No en el valle

Some days nothing grows and nobody comes: **no hay nada en el huerto**, **no hay nadie en la tienda**, **nunca llueve en verano**. For neither this nor that, use ni: **no tengo ni semillas ni dinero**.

vocabulary.example: No hay nada en el huerto todavía.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There's nothing in the garden yet.

vocabulary.example: No hay nadie en la tienda.
No tengo ni semillas ni dinero.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I have neither seeds nor money.

vocabulary.example: No hay nada en el huerto todavía.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There's nothing in the garden yet.

bites.title: No en el valle
bites.rule: No goes before the verb and the sentence stays negative: no hay nada, no hay nadie, no pesco nunca.
bites.example: No hay nadie en la tienda y no tengo nada de dinero.
bites.example_meaning: There's nobody at the shop and I have no money at all.

listening.text: Las fresas no están listas todavía.

listening.meaning: Nobody is working on the farm today.

listening.meaning: Rosa has no money for seeds.

sorts.why: Algo, alguien and siempre are positive; nada, nadie and nunca are their negatives.

rustwake.content:
## No en el páramo

Out here nothing works and nobody comes: **no hay nada en la gasolinera**, **no hay nadie en la antena**, **nunca camino de noche**. For neither this nor that, use ni: **no tengo ni agua ni tuercas**.

vocabulary.example: No hay nada en la gasolinera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There's nothing at the petrol station.

vocabulary.example: No hay nadie en la antena.
Nunca escucho la radio de los bandidos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I never listen to the bandits' radio.
I don't have any nuts either.

vocabulary.example: No tengo ni agua ni tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I have neither water nor nuts.

vocabulary.example: Siempre hay polvo, pero hoy no hay tormenta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There's always dust, but today there's no storm.
I don't have a single nut.

vocabulary.example: No hay ningún tónico en la mochila.
vocabulary.example_meaning: There are no tonics in the backpack.

vocabulary.example: Nunca camino por el páramo de noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I never walk through the wasteland at night.

bites.title: No en el páramo
bites.rule: No goes before the verb and the sentence stays negative: no hay nada, no hay nadie, no camino nunca. Out here nothing works and nobody comes.
bites.example: No hay nadie en la gasolinera y no tengo ninguna tuerca.
bites.example_meaning: There's nobody at the petrol station and I don't have a single nut.

listening.text: En el taller no hay nada.
listening.meaning: There's nothing in the workshop.

listening.text: Marta no tiene ninguna tuerca hoy.
listening.meaning: Marta doesn't have a single nut today.
listening.note: New word: la tuerca = nut (the wasteland money).

listening.text: Leo nunca explora el páramo solo.
listening.meaning: Leo never explores the wasteland alone.
listening.note: New word: el páramo = the wasteland.

listening.text: No hay ni agua ni gaseosa Zafiro en el mercado.
listening.meaning: There's neither water nor Zafiro soda at the market.
listening.note: Ni … ni after no: neither … nor.

listening.text: Yo tampoco tengo tónicos.
listening.meaning: I don't have tonics either.

Nunca camino por el páramo de noche.
